title: Отказ Нагиева и приглашение Елены  (Nagiyev's Refusal and Inviting Elena)

segments.t: In the office, Nagiyev thinks Max is joking when the young cook asks to borrow money and sends him away empty-handed. Back in the kitchen, Chef Barinov calls Elena Pavlovna to announce that the apartment is completely free for the evening.
Елена Павловна, у меня мама на балет ушла.
Let's replay the exchange and look closely at each Russian phrase.
'I do not understand.' Because she does not understand, Elena treats the matter as settled.

'In that sense?' With the conversation and moment hanging in the air, Kostya puts Elena on the spot. In Russian, he does not need helper words like "do" or "did"—rising pitch alone turns it into a question.
'For sheer nerve.' With the shift and apartment in play, Elena keeps this short reply brisk and direct.
'What is with you?' By asking what with Elena is, Kostya presses Elena for a straight answer. Speaking with the close, informal "you" strips away any polite distance between them.
'I was only joking.' Pointing out that she was only joking gives Kostya a sobering reality check.
'Does he know how to talk?' Asking whether he know how to talk is how Kostya puts Elena on the spot.

'Stepan Andreyevich?' With the work and moment hanging in the air, Elena puts Kostya on the spot. In Russian, she does not need helper words like "do" or "did"—rising pitch alone turns it into a question.
Елена Павловна, у меня мама на балет ушла.

'Elena Pavlovna, my mother has gone out to the ballet.' Noting that his mother has gone out to the ballet keeps Kostya's side of the story simple and clear. In Russian you say "by me" or "with us" rather than "I have", so the situation sits right with the person.
'Why walk on foot?' With the point and apartment hanging in the air, Elena puts Kostya on the spot.

'What I meant to say was...' When Kostya asks if what he meant to say was, Elena has to answer fast. In Russian, he does not need helper words like "do" or "did"—rising pitch alone turns it into a question.

'Really? Sounds good?' With the point and shift hanging in the air, Elena puts Kostya on the spot. In Russian, she does not need helper words like "do" or "did"—rising pitch alone turns it into a question.
'Well then, what do you say?' By asking what Elena says, Kostya presses Elena for a straight answer.
'See you soon.' Elena explains that Kostya should see Kostya soon, keeping her voice calm and direct. Let's hear the complete conversation once more.
Елена Павловна, у меня мама на балет ушла.

That wraps up this scene as nagiyev laughs off Max's request for a loan, while Chef Barinov calls Elena Pavlovna to invite her to his apartment now that his mother is at the ballet. See you next time!
